text:
sasha: heads up — noticed nondeterministic evals for the new quantized-v2 model on the sampling benchmark. same commit, same seed, different outputs ~15% of the time.

mike: ugh, when did this start? recent deploy?

sasha: started after the resume-cutoff patch that lets the runner stream partial batches. suspect the cutoff logic advances the sampler RNG differently across resume boundaries.

ana: can you paste a minimal repro?

sasha: yep. run locally: `./tools/eval_runner --model=models/quantized-v2 --sampler=top_p --top_p=0.92 --temp=0.7 --cutoff=128 --batch-size=4 --seed=420042` run twice back-to-back and compare outputs. I get mismatch tokens at around token 70-85.

lee: interesting — I repro with your exact flags. logs show sampler state serialized on resume with `pos=72` but worker resumes with `pos=71` once in a while.

rachel: that off-by-one would desync the RNG stream and cause completely different samples, especially with top_p interleaving.

mike: is the serialization using token-count or byte-offset? we had a prior bug where tokenization differences across quant kernels changed counts slightly.

sasha: serialization uses token-count. but the quantized tokenizer fallback path returns a different special-token mapping in some workloads — so token counts can differ during warmup.

ci-bot: CI Job #4821 failed: `eval-sampling-stability` — flaky mismatch (detected by checksum).

ana: log snippet: ```
[runner] checkpointing sampler state: rng_state_len=2048 pos=72
[worker] resuming from checkpoint: rng_state_len=2048 pos=71
```

lee: that confirms the mismatch. hypothesis: during streaming resume we reconstruct inputs and re-tokenize; on quant kernels the tokenizer uses the loaded vocab variant which maps an unk differently causing a -1 token shift on resume path.

mike: workarounds? force using baseline tokenizer across resume, or include the tokenized prefix in the checkpoint so resume doesn't re-tokenize.

rachel: suggestion: (1) make resume read and reuse the exact tokenized prefix from the checkpoint; (2) add a short deterministic-sampling mode for evals that consumes RNG deterministically even across resume boundaries; (3) add a small CI deterministic test that runs 8 seeds and diffs outputs.

sasha: I'll open a PR with (1) and (2). plan: checkpoint schema v2 includes `prefix_tokens` and `sampler_ticks` so resume replays tokens without re-tokenizing. also adding a `--deterministic` flag for eval_runner that seeds per-request RNG and forbids any fallback seeding.

ana: also add debug telemetry: echo `seed_id` and `sampler_pos` in each sample output so CI can assert.

mike: can we also guard against quantized tokenizer variants? maybe add an assert in model-onboard pipeline that vocab hash must match serving tokenizer hash.

lee: good call. we'll add `tokenizer_hash` to model metadata and fail model bring-up if it doesn't match the runtime kernel.

rachel: created ISSUE-1189 for CI test additions and model metadata checks.

sasha: PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/pull/204 — includes tests and a small perf microbenchmark for prefix checkpointing.

mike: running the new tests locally now. initial run: 8 seeds, all stable. will let CI run full matrix.

ci-bot: CI Job #4830 started: `eval-sampling-stability` with PR #204.

lee: long term we should add a fuzz harness that mutates tokenizers and quant kernels to catch these alignment problems before onboard.

rachel: agreed. for now, add a quick gating check: `onboard` job must run sampling-stability with `--deterministic` against baseline example prompts.

sasha: thanks team — moving to hotfix. will monitor flakes for next 48h and revert resume patch if needed. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks — ping once CI green and we'll merge.

ci-bot: CI Job #4830 passed: `eval-sampling-stability` (PR #204).
